selectionEntries.name: List Builder Disclaimer

rules.name: A companion to the army rules
rules.description: The listbuilder is designed to sit alongside the army rules PDF, not replace it. Players are expected to consult the army rules during list construction, including unit rules and weapon profiles, and the listbuilder actively encourages this through its presentation.

rules.name: Simple, intuitive, and focused on meaningful choices
rules.description: The listbuilder is simple, readable, and intuitive. It represents the choices players actually make when recording an army, rather than reproducing every procedural step used by the army rules PDF. This keeps the common 99% of list construction fast and clear. Exceptional cases can be resolved using the army rules PDF, which the player is already expected to have open.

rules.name: Clear feedback on illegal list construction
rules.description: The listbuilder reliably identifies illegal list-building actions and clearly communicates what makes them invalid.

rules.name: A fancy notepad, not a rules engine
rules.description: At its core, the listbuilder replaces the notepad where a player would normally record what they are taking. It helps the player record their choices as quickly and simply as possible.

selectionEntries.comment: Permanent informational Configuration entry. This is player-facing guidance for how the listbuilder is intended to be used. It is inserted by default but intentionally has no min/max constraints because its presence/quantity is not a semantic roster rule.

rules.name: Army List - 800 Points
rules.description:
Rapid & lethal - this is the size for quick action. 1-2 hours.
You can only bring two leader units.
For each non-Rare unit in the Other section, the first copy costs its normal points; each additional copy costs 20 additional points.

rules.name: Army List - 1200 Points
rules.description:
Bold, tactical play is key at this size as you adapt to the dice and the battlefield. This is the
recommended size for 1v1 games. 2-3 hours.
You can only bring three leader units.
For each non-Rare unit in the Other section, the first two copies cost their normal points; each additional copy costs 20 additional points.

rules.name: Army List - 1600pts
rules.description:
Strategy takes the spotlight as you battle to extend advantages over the long term. 3+ hours.
You can only bring four leader units.
For each non-Rare unit in the Other section, the first three copies cost their normal points; each additional copy costs 20 additional points.

gameSystem.comment:
SEMANTIC SOURCE OF TRUTH

The Universal Unit Skeleton (UUS) is the semantic source of truth.

New Recruit is an output format. The compiler MUST NOT invent additional game meaning merely because New Recruit requires a particular data shape.

If a UUS rule cannot be compiled deterministically, fail loudly rather than inventing faction-specific behavior.

Preserve the player's decision structure, not merely the final legality of the roster.

Stable source IDs MUST be preferred wherever they exist. Display names, array positions, and presentation order MUST NOT become surrogate semantic IDs.


CATEGORY ARCHITECTURE

New Recruit categories MUST NOT be treated as the semantic source of unit identity.

Categories are divided into two classes:

Presentation Categories

Visible to the player.
May be used as primary categories.
Determine organization in the New Recruit builder.
MUST NOT be relied upon for list-building semantics.

Internal Semantic Categories

Used only where New Recruit requires or benefits from grouping multiple semantic objects.
MUST be hidden from the player where possible.
MUST NOT be primary categories.
MUST NOT determine where a unit appears in the builder.
MUST describe genuine reusable semantic sets, not one-off implementation accidents.

Prefer direct stable-ID references over creating an internal category when a rule refers to specific named objects.

Attachment behavior MUST be represented through attachment/Association semantics, not inferred from presentation category.

Unit limits MUST derive from UUS semantic fields such as unit_class, counts_toward_unit_type_limit, restrictions and list-building effects, not from the unit's visible New Recruit category.


GAME SIZE AND POINTS LIMITS

The New Recruit Points cost type MUST have no preselected roster cost limit.

Players MUST NOT be required to specify an army points limit when creating a roster.

The Points cost type therefore uses an unlimited/default limit (-1).

Army size is selected after roster creation through the mandatory Game Size configuration choice.

The available Game Size options are:

800 Points (Quick)
1200 Points (Standard)
1600 Points (Long)

The selected Game Size is the semantic source of all game-size-dependent list-building restrictions, including army-size rules, unit-copy costs and Leader limits.

The generic New Recruit roster cost-limit field MUST NOT be treated as authoritative game-size information.

If a dynamic roster-points ceiling cannot be represented reliably in New Recruit, do not fake it. Keep Game Size as the semantic source and leave the generic Points limit unlimited until the mechanic is proven.


LISTBUILDER PRESENTATION PHILOSOPHY

The listbuilder is a companion to the army rules PDF and a fancy notepad, not a replacement rules engine.

Represent the choices players actually make when recording an army.

Do not reproduce procedural replacement wording merely because the PDF expresses a final loadout through a sequence of "replace X with Y" instructions.

Prefer a direct final-state choice when it preserves the real list-building decision.

The common 99% path SHOULD be quick and obvious. Exceptional edge cases may rely on the army rules PDF when reproducing them would materially worsen the list-building interface.

When there is tension between literal procedural wording and a clean exact representation of the final choice, prefer the clean exact representation.

Do not hide point costs or create invisible taxes. Any points added by the builder MUST remain visible to the player.


UNIT ORDERING AND PLAYER-FACING NAMES

Root units MUST appear in the same order as their army rules PDF unless a specific design decision says otherwise. Use stable Position/sortIndex values to preserve this order.

Use the proper in-universe model or role name whenever one exists.

For infantry model groups, prefer:
1. Proper role/title, such as Sister Superior, Exarch, Justicar, Klaivex, Shas'vre.
2. Faction-specific model noun.
3. Singular/plural unit model noun.
4. Generic "Model N" only as an absolute fallback.

A sergeant/champion occupies the first model position for numbering purposes. If a unit contains a named sergeant followed by numbered models, the next ordinary model is Model 2, not Model 1.

Do not invent a sergeant title when the unit has no distinct sergeant loadout to record.


LOADOUT UI GRAMMAR

Use these top-level section names consistently:
- Loadout Options
- Special Weapon Loadouts
- Paid Wargear
- Additional Models
- Additional Leader

Omit sections that do not apply.

Mandatory exclusive choices SHOULD normally use min 1 / max 1 and default to the first normal/legal option.

Do NOT create a default if doing so can open the unit in an illegal state. In that case, prefer an optional 0/1 presentation with a built-in (None) state and validate completion separately with a constructive custom error.

Fixed equipment may be represented as a one-option mandatory group when displaying it materially improves the recorded loadout.

For vehicles, do not invent artificial headers such as Hull, Turret, Pintle or Sponson merely to label otherwise self-explanatory weapon lists.

For mechs or large models, physical slot headers such as Right Arm, Left Arm, Shoulder Weapon 1 or Heavy Weapon 2 are appropriate when the physical slot explains the decision.

Do not add invisible wrapper groups merely to force a particular collapse/indentation behavior. Empty visual wrappers have previously produced blank gaps and poor New Recruit UI.


SERGEANTS, CHAMPIONS AND SPECIALIST MODELS

When a sergeant/champion has a distinct loadout, represent that model directly under its proper title and place it first.

Do not pretend a sergeant/champion starts as an ordinary model and then "upgrades" into its actual equipment.

If a free specialist replacement is effectively the intended identity of a model slot, represent that specialist directly and omit ordinary fallback equipment when the fallback would only advertise a non-meaningful choice.

If the specialist option costs points, retain the ordinary fallback state because declining the paid upgrade is a meaningful list-building choice.

When the source allows up to X specialist selections and repetition is allowed, prefer X independent model/choice slots over a quantity spinner.

When a unit-wide cap can be enforced cleanly by making an option disappear after the cap is reached, this is preferred to a post-hoc error.

Conditional hiding MUST NOT create a state where an already-selected option later becomes hidden. New Recruit treats selected-hidden entries as invalid. Use disappearing options only when the hidden entry is an unselected alternative.


PAID WARGEAR

Paid Wargear is for additive equipment or abilities whose ownership does not need to be tracked on a specific physical model.

If taking the option requires a model to lose or replace existing equipment, the paid option belongs inline on the affected model's loadout, not as unit-level Paid Wargear.

Unmodelled additive wargear, grenades, cherubs, smoke launchers, icons, bombs and similar unit-level bookkeeping SHOULD normally be represented at unit level.

A single paid item MUST NOT be placed directly as a selectable child under Paid Wargear if New Recruit renders that shape as a quantity spinner.

Instead, place each paid item inside its own optional max-1 selection group so the UI renders a clean (None) / option choice.

If a unit may take the same class of paid upgrade multiple times and model identity is not important, prefer multiple independent optional slots rather than a quantity spinner.

If model identity matters, place the paid option inline on the eligible model slots.

Ability-only paid wargear MUST include the full exact player-facing ability text on the selection.


RULE TEXT AUTHORING

When player-facing rule text is available in the authoritative army rules PDF, preserve it verbatim.

Do not paraphrase attachment wording, Leader Capacity wording, or ability-only wargear text when the exact wording is available.

If exact wording is unavailable, do not invent a synthetic rule and present it as authoritative.

Rules that are already fully represented by a weapon/profile name do not need their full weapon mechanics duplicated in the listbuilder.

The listbuilder SHOULD include full text for selections whose mechanical identity is primarily a named ability rather than a weapon/profile.


VARIABLE UNIT SIZE

When practical, represent the minimum legal unit size in the root unit cost and add larger sizes through Additional Models.

Additional models SHOULD be explicit model entries with their own point cost and loadout subtree when they have meaningful individual choices.

Avoid quantity spinners for additional models when a clearer model-entry presentation is available.

Sequential/nested optional additional-model entries MAY be used when extra models are identical and nesting produces a clearer 4/5/6-style progression than a quantity control.

Do not leave a Phase 0.1 minimum-size shell comment once proper variable-size controls have been implemented.


ATTACHMENTS AND NESTED LEADERS

Normal Leaders that must join a host SHOULD use the established required Association pattern:
- Leader-side association min 1 / max 1.
- Eligible host units carry hidden "May Attach To: X" semantic categories.
- Eligible hosts enforce their normal attachment capacity.

Every Leader SHOULD also display the exact player-facing attachment rule text from the PDF.

A Countless or host-local Leader that is conceptually selected as part of its host MAY use the Additional Leader pattern instead of appearing as a floating root Leader.

Additional Leader is especially appropriate when:
- the Leader does not consume normal Leader capacity,
- the Leader may coexist with a normal attached Leader,
- and there is no meaningful reason for the player to select the Leader before selecting its host.

Nested Leader units retain their own complete unit/loadout tree.

Nested units may themselves be valid association targets. This has been proven and may be used when it makes the roster easier to understand.

When a rule grants required/free child units, a Neuroloid-style nested generated unit is preferred over asking the player to create and then associate the granted unit manually, provided the nested child remains fully configurable.


ADDITIONAL COPY COSTS

The Game System owns the reusable semantic category and shared player-facing rules for Additional Copy Costs.

The catalogue owns the per-unit arithmetic because copy counting references catalogue-local unit IDs.

The current generic rule applies only to native non-Rare units in the Other section:
- 800 Points: first 1 copy costs normal points.
- 1200 Points: first 2 copies cost normal points.
- 1600 Points: first 3 copies cost normal points.
- Each additional identical copy costs +20 Points.

Rare units retain their hard max-1 rule unless their source semantics say otherwise.

Troops have no generic copy ceiling from this system.

Affected units SHOULD:
- remove the old 1/2/3 hard-copy constraint,
- gain the hidden Counts Toward Other Soft Copy Cost semantic category,
- link the shared unit reminder rule.

Each catalogue SHOULD own one permanent required Additional Copy Costs Configuration entry that visibly aggregates the surcharge.

Never apply this surcharge invisibly to unit costs in a way the player cannot identify.


ERROR MESSAGE AUTHORING CONVENTION

Prefer structurally preventing an illegal choice when that can be done without making the UI harder to understand.

If structural prevention would make the interface awkward, keep the cleaner input shape and validate the semantic rule separately.

Custom validation errors MUST use player-facing game terminology.

Do not expose New Recruit implementation vocabulary such as:
- association
- selection
- constraint
- child
- parent

Every player-facing error SHOULD communicate:
1. What is wrong.
2. Why the list is illegal.
3. What the player can do to fix it.

When possible, the relevant unit/rule entry SHOULD also contain enough rule text for the player to understand the repair without leaving the builder.

STANDARD ERROR LANGUAGE TEMPLATES

missing_required_choice
"{UNIT} is missing a required {CHOICE}. Select {FIX}."

incomplete_model_loadout
"{UNIT} has one or more models without {CHOICE}. Select one {OPTIONS} for each {MODEL}."

too_many_identical_choices
"{UNIT} may include no more than {MAX} {OPTION}. Change one of the selected {OPTION} choices."

missing_attachment
"{LEADER} must be attached to {HOSTS}. Add an eligible unit to your army, then select it under Attaches To."

leader_host_limit
"{HOST} cannot have more than {MAX} {LEADER_TYPE}. Remove or move one of the attached leaders."

rare_limit
"Your army may include only one {UNIT} because it is Rare. Remove the additional copy."

missing_granted_units
"{UNIT} requires {COUNT} {GRANTED_UNIT} at {GAME_SIZE}. Add the required units and select/configure them under {CONTROL}. {EXTRA_INSTRUCTION}"

invalid_unit_size
"{UNIT} must contain {MIN}-{MAX} models. Add or remove models until the unit is within this range."

These templates are authoring standards, not necessarily shared New Recruit objects. Catalogue-local modifiers may reference catalogue-local IDs while reusing the standardized language.

Proven reference pattern:
For a complex mandatory loadout where legal defaults cannot be chosen automatically, allow a visible (None) state and use a semantic counter plus a custom error until every required model is configured.


REUSABLE SHARED UNIT CONTENT

When complete playable unit trees are reused across multiple armies, compile a dedicated shared library and use thin host-specific entryLinks.

Do not duplicate the full unit tree into every host catalogue merely because New Recruit permits it.

Do not import an entire playable faction catalogue when only reusable unit content is needed.

The shared compiled library is still an output artifact. The UUS remains the semantic source of truth.


PREFER DIRECT REPRESENTATION OVER ARTIFICIAL CODIFICATION

The compiler MUST choose the simplest exact New Recruit representation for each semantic rule.

Repeated local constraints, conditions, modifiers, or explicit unit references are acceptable, even when they occur on many objects.

Shared categories, tags, helper entries, or other abstractions SHOULD be introduced only when they represent a meaningful reusable concept or materially simplify the resulting implementation.

The number of objects affected is not, by itself, a reason to create or avoid an abstraction.

Do not create a keyword merely because several objects happen to share the same implementation.

Do not duplicate logic merely because only one object currently uses an existing meaningful concept.

Prefer whichever representation has fewer dependencies, less indirection, and clearer correspondence to the UUS semantics.


CATALOGUE DATA AUTHORING CONVENTION: DETERMINISTIC IDS

All AI-authored or compiler-generated catalogue objects MUST use deterministic IDs.

ID algorithm

Construct the object's canonical semantic path.
Canonical paths MUST describe semantic identity, never array position, display order, or other incidental structure.
Where stable source IDs exist, such as UUS unit IDs, model-group IDs, selection-group IDs, option IDs, or configuration IDs, those IDs MUST be used in the canonical path rather than display names.
The path MUST identify the object type and enough semantic ancestry to uniquely identify the object.
Convert the complete path to lowercase.
Use / as the separator.
Hash the UTF-8 path using SHA-256.
Take the first 16 hexadecimal characters.
Format as xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx.

Existing catalogue IDs are authoritative and MUST NOT be regenerated.
References to existing objects MUST reuse their existing IDs.
Only newly created catalogue objects receive deterministic IDs.
Every distinct object MUST have exactly one distinct canonical semantic path.
Compiler-generated helper objects MUST use paths describing their semantic purpose, not numeric counters or creation order.
Renaming an existing object does NOT automatically change its ID.
If two distinct objects produce the same canonical path, compilation MUST fail.
If two different canonical paths produce the same deterministic ID, compilation MUST fail.
Never resolve references by display name when an ID exists.
Never generate random IDs for AI-authored or compiler-generated catalogue data.


GAME SYSTEM ID STABILITY

Game System IDs do not need to be regenerated deterministically.
Once a Game System object is adopted into the canonical system, its ID is authoritative and MUST remain stable because faction catalogues may reference it.
New AI-authored Game System objects MAY use deterministic IDs as a safe default, but deterministic regeneration of existing Game System IDs is not required or desired.


FUTURE SHARED CONTENT CATEGORIES

The Game System defines visible presentation categories for:
- Great Traitors’ Arsenal
- Left Hand of the Emperor

These categories are infrastructure only. They do not currently define eligibility, copy limits, attachment rules, import behavior, or any other game semantics. Future shared libraries/catalogues may link eligible units into these presentation categories while keeping the UUS as the semantic source of truth.


LIST BUILDER DISCLAIMER

The Game System owns a permanent List Builder Disclaimer Configuration entry.

It is positioned before Game Size and is intended to remain visible in every faction catalogue that uses this Game System.

The disclaimer is player-facing guidance. It MUST NOT become a semantic source for compiler behavior.


COMMENT AND REVISION HYGIENE

Game System and catalogue comments are authoring documentation.

Use comments to record durable conventions, implementation rationale, known engine behavior, and intentional simplifications.

Prefer recording reusable standards in the Game System comment and unit/faction-specific exceptions in catalogue or unit comments.

Do not duplicate large generic conventions into every catalogue.

A comment-only documentation change does not require a Game System revision bump.

Bump the Game System revision when a referenced Game System object, rule, category, force structure, cost type, or other executable/player-visible Game System data changes.

CONFIGURATION VALIDATION PATTERNS

Purely informational Configuration entries that are inserted by default, such as List Builder Disclaimer, SHOULD NOT carry min/max constraints when their absence or duplication does not change roster legality.

Semantic/accounting Configuration entries are different: if their quantity affects points or legality, they MUST remain protected against accidental deletion or duplication, preferably with constructive custom errors rather than stock New Recruit implementation-language errors.

LEADER CAPACITY ERROR PATTERN

Counts Toward Leader Maximum is a hidden semantic counting category only.

Do not place the roster max constraint directly on that category, because New Recruit reports errors in implementation language such as:
"Army has N selections too many of Counts Toward Leader Maximum (max X)."

Instead, Game Size owns the shared player-facing Leader Capacity validator.

At 800 / 1200 / 1600 Points, a custom error triggers when the count of selections in Counts Toward Leader Maximum exceeds 2 / 3 / 4 respectively.

Standard wording:
"Your army has too many Leaders that count toward Leader Capacity. At {GAME_SIZE}, you may include at most {MAX} such Leaders. Remove a Leader or replace one with a Leader that does not count toward Leader Capacity."

This is a universal Game System error and SHOULD NOT be reimplemented independently in faction catalogues.

AUTOMATIC CONFIGURATION DUPLICATE TEMPLATE

For catalogue-owned automatic accounting entries that must exist exactly once, suppress the stock max-1 error where practical and use:
"{ENTRY} is automatically managed by the listbuilder and should appear only once. Remove any extra {ENTRY} entries."

If the entry must also be protected against deletion, preserve or separately replace its minimum validation until a constructive missing-entry validator exists.


REQUIRED CONFIGURATION VALIDATION — REV10 TEST

This revision tests parent-level missing Configuration validation on the Army > Configuration category link. Game Size and Additional Copy Costs validate their own duplicate copies with custom errors. The Configuration category link validates missing Game Size directly and missing Additional Copy Costs through the hidden "Required Additional Copy Costs Configuration" semantic category. This presentation behavior must be confirmed in New Recruit before being treated as a proven authoring standard.

ROAMING CATEGORY VALIDATION (REV11)
Roaming Leader and Roaming Troop are presentation/semantic categories only and no longer carry shared max-1 constraints. Consumer catalogue mechanics such as Drukhari Roaming Performers own their own constructive limits so player-facing errors can be attached to the rule/configuration object responsible for them.

sharedRules.name: Additional Copy Costs
sharedRules.description:
PROTOTYPE — NON-RARE OTHER UNITS
At 800 Points, the first copy of each affected unit costs its normal points. At 1200 Points, the first two copies cost their normal points. At 1600 Points, the first three copies cost their normal points. Each additional copy of that same unit costs 20 additional points.
The total surcharge is applied automatically to the Additional Copy Costs Configuration entry.

sharedRules.name: Additional Copy Costs
sharedRules.description: This unit uses the Additional Copy Costs rule. Copies beyond the normal allowance for the selected Game Size cost 20 additional points each.
